title: About & references
text:
About this draft
This v0.1 methodological discussion draft presents a causal-assumption framework linking a directed acyclic graph (DAG), an assumption register, and a Summary of Evidence table (SET). The templates, terminology, and reporting examples are proposals for review, not validated guidance or adopted standards. The Briefing sets out the four feedback questions.

title: About & references
text:
Methodological context
Turner RM, Spiegelhalter DJ, Smith GCS, Thompson SG. Bias modelling in evidence synthesis. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series A. 2009;172(1):21–47. Read the paper.
The proposed framework is a qualitative counterpart to quantitative bias modelling: it makes causal structure, stream-specific contributions, connecting assumptions, and possible shared biases explicit. It does not estimate bias parameters or replace quantitative adjustment.

title: About & references
text:
Applications and evidence

TAAR1: retrospective illustration
The TAAR1 example reconstructs how the framework could have supported a completed review. Its diagram, assumption IDs, and statuses are illustrative retrospective judgements, not records of the original panel using these tools.
The worked SET reports estimates and 95% confidence intervals from the published triangulation and the living systematic review. It is not a current evidence update or an independent audit of those publications.


LSR8: ongoing application
For Heat & Mental Health, the framework is being introduced after protocol completion, while the living systematic reviews are underway. Proposed assumptions and priority adjudications remain open for review; they are not completed meeting conclusions.

title: About & references
text:
Templates and figures
The protocol proposals reproduce proposed additions to the associations v3.2 and hypothesis-generating v2.2 templates. Extracts and blank working templates are available on the relevant proposal pages; the original internal Word drafts are not distributed here.
The TAAR1 DAG is a simplified reconstruction highlighting selected assumptions; its proxy connection is not a physical causal arrow. The six LSR8 diagrams reproduce the draft v1.1 figures without redrawing. The deliverables schematic illustrates the proposed workflow, not a causal model. Diagrams express assumptions to examine, not established effects.

title: Proposal 2 · Triangulation meeting worksheet
text:
Purpose
The worksheet gives the panel a common record of how evidence changes its interpretation of the DAG and its assumptions. The Summary of Evidence table (SET) summarises the evidence; the assumption register records the conditions attached to the interpretation.
See the TAAR1 DAG and register for the worked illustration. The worksheet below turns that reasoning into prompts a meeting can use.

title: Proposal 2 · Triangulation meeting worksheet
text:
Four steps







Step
What the team records




1. Map
The relationship or query each stream informs, the estimate or finding, and the assumptions needed to connect it to the target question.


2. Compare
Whether the questions, populations, measures, and timescales are comparable; where findings agree or diverge.


3. Examine bias
Shared and differing bias mechanisms, their expected directions, and the implications for interpretation.


4. Revise and record
The conclusion and its conditions; changes to assumptions or the diagram; unresolved questions and actions.

title: Proposal 2 · Triangulation meeting worksheet
text:
Proposed worksheet fields







Before the discussion
After the discussion




Target question; date and participants; diagram, register, and SET versions; evidence already known when the framework was adopted.
Conclusion and conditions; revised versions; actions, owners, and review dates.



The Word worksheet provides blank tables and response spaces for these fields and the four steps. It can be completed before and during a meeting, then kept with the review records.


Detailed questions for follow-up


Which fields are essential for the panel, and which can be prepared or maintained elsewhere?
Is the preparation and recording burden justified, and who owns the record between updates?


The four questions on the Briefing page guide the meeting discussion.

title: Concepts: the terms needed for this proposal
text:
The argument
The proposed unit of reasoning is target relationship → stream-specific contribution → connecting assumptions. A cross-stream judgement needs to specify what each stream informs and the conditions under which its findings bear on the target question. Shared bias remains a possible explanation for apparent agreement.
The framework extends familiar within-study DAG reasoning to this between-stream setting. The DAG shows the proposed causal structure; the register records the connecting assumptions; the Summary of Evidence table (SET) links the findings to them. Its role as a qualitative counterpart to quantitative bias modelling is explained in the Briefing.

title: Concepts: the terms needed for this proposal
text:
A worked illustration
The TAAR1 example shows the DAG and its assumption register together. Selected labels identify the proxy connection and the proposed mechanism. The worked evidence summary shows how the register links enter the SET.

title: Concepts: the terms needed for this proposal
text:
Seven terms for this discussion







Term
Working definition




Causal DAG — directed acyclic graph
A diagram of hypothesised direct causal influences, with no directed cycles. Both arrows and omitted arrows encode assumptions.


Assumption register
A versioned record of assumptions with IDs, statements, affected relationships/streams, judgements, rationale, and what could challenge them.


Proxy
A measured variable used to stand in for another construct. Its relevance needs justification; the animal behavioural outcome and human symptom outcome remain distinct.


Estimand
The precise quantity sought: for example, a treatment contrast in a specified population, outcome, and follow-up.


Indirectness / applicability
A difference between the evidence and the target population, exposure/intervention, outcome, timing, or setting that affects its relevance.


SET — Summary of Evidence table
A concise account of findings, bias, applicability, and the assumptions relevant to triangulation.


Bias type — offset versus scaling
Offset (additive / shift) bias adds a distortion and can move a true null. Scaling (proportional / stretch) bias multiplies an effect on the stated scale; a true zero remains zero on that scale.

title: Concepts: the terms needed for this proposal
text:
Reference appendix


Additional methodological terms

These definitions retain the rest of the source glossary for reference.







Term
Working definition




Node
A variable in the diagram, such as exposure, a mediator, or an outcome.


Edge / arrow
An assumed direct causal influence between two nodes. A target question can concern several paths rather than one arrow.


Direct versus total effect
A direct effect excludes pathways through specified mediators; a total effect includes pathways through them. A trial’s total-effect estimate should not automatically be attached to a direct arrow.


Confounder
A variable that causally influences both exposure and outcome, creating a non-causal route between them.


Effect modifier
A characteristic across whose values an effect differs on a specified scale. It is not necessarily a confounder.


Mediator
A variable on a causal pathway, such as exposure → mediator → outcome. Adjusting for it can change the quantity being estimated.


Collider
A variable caused by two other variables. Conditioning on it can open a non-causal path.


Scoping mode versus hypothesis mode
Scoping mode uses the diagram to clarify the question and evidence contributions. Hypothesis mode makes proposed pathways explicit for examination. Record the diagram’s purpose and when it was introduced.


SMD — standardised mean difference
An effect expressed in standard-deviation units. Similar units do not make different outcomes or target quantities equivalent.


Bias direction — towards or away from the null
How a bias is expected to move an estimate relative to the true value, for a specified contrast and scale. Direction may be uncertain or involve crossing the null.


Triangulation
Drawing an interpretation across evidence contributions while examining their different and shared key sources of bias and assumptions.


Orthogonality / differing bias structures
The extent to which key bias mechanisms differ across streams. Independence needs justification; different design labels alone do not establish it.


Causal-assumption framework (“scaffolding”)
The proposed structure connecting the DAG, explicit assumptions, evidence summaries, meeting deliberation, and reporting.


Assumption types
Four proposed categories: structural, identifying, proxy, and indirectness/applicability, defined below.


Structural assumption
A claim about a causal relationship or its absence, such as the proposed dopamine pathway in TAAR1 (A3).


Identifying assumption
A condition needed for a study’s estimate to identify the stated causal quantity, such as sufficient confounding control for an observational contrast.


Proxy assumption
A claim that a measured proxy is informative about the target construct, such as the contested TAAR1 animal-to-human connection (A1).


Indirectness assumption
A claim about the extent to which findings transfer to the target population, intervention/exposure, outcome, or setting.


Target relationship / causal query
The question the review seeks to answer. It may concern an association, a total effect, a direct effect, or a mediated pathway.


Evidence stream
Evidence grouped by a relevant design or inferential approach; distinct identifying assumptions can require separate streams.


Evidence contribution map
A table showing what each stream can inform and which assumptions connect it to the target question.


Decision log
A dated record of changes, reasons, and ownership, linking successive diagram and register versions.

title: Making causal assumptions explicit in triangulation
text:
The problem
Cross-stream agreement in triangulation is currently interpreted without making explicit the causal structure, proxy validity, and applicability assumptions that connect each stream to the target question — and shared biases can manufacture apparent agreement.

title: Making causal assumptions explicit in triangulation
text:
The conceptual claim to stress-test

Target relationship → Stream-specific contribution → Connecting assumptions

This is the unit of reasoning I want the team to stress-test: whether it captures what warrants a cross-stream judgement, including when shared bias could explain agreement. The methodological aim is to make that reasoning explicit and reviewable; the templates are its practical application.

title: Making causal assumptions explicit in triangulation
text:
Where this sits methodologically
Directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) are familiar tools for making the assumptions behind confounding control within a study explicit. This proposal extends that logic to the between-stream setting: which target relationship each stream informs, and which identifying, proxy, and applicability assumptions connect its contribution to that target.

title: Making causal assumptions explicit in triangulation
section: What I mean by the framework
text:
What I mean by the framework
The working notes call this “scaffolding”: a linked set of visual and written tools that helps a team make its assumptions explicit and carry its reasoning between stages of a review.
The DAG visualises the hypothesised causal structure. An assumption register records the assumptions, their rationale, and what could challenge them. The Summary of Evidence table (SET) connects the findings to those assumptions. The three templates guide how the team prepares, discusses, and reports this information.
See the worked TAAR1 DAG and register →



Three proposed deliverables — protocol templates, a meeting worksheet, and reporting with a SET — and the reasoning each supports.

title: Proposal 1 · Update protocol templates
text:
Why update the templates?
The associations workflow produces a Summary of Evidence table (SET). The hypothesis-generating workflow already recommends a DAG and produces a Summary of Evidence on Mediators (SEM). The amendments connect the causal diagram, assumption register, and meeting record across both routes.
The retrospective TAAR1 example motivates the proposed changes:







Gap illustrated by the retrospective example
What the amendment addresses




Association and mechanism questions can occur in the same review.
Declare the review mode and the diagram’s purpose.


Pathways may be reconstructed after the findings.
Record the proposed structure and challenge conditions before synthesis.


The two template routes produce different evidence summaries.
Link both routes to the DAG and assumption register.


Meeting reasoning may remain implicit.
Preserve the assumptions, judgements, and revisions in a reusable record.

title: Proposal 1 · Update protocol templates
text:
What changes in each template?
The uploaded drafts frame all additions as recommendations. These practical prompts are a main methods contribution for review.








Template
Where the additions appear
Practical change proposed




Associations v3.2 draft
Research questions; reporting bias; evidence summary; triangulation meeting.
Declare the review mode, introduce a versioned DAG and register, record bias direction, and use the assumptions in meeting conclusions.


Hypothesis-generating v2.2 draft
DAG guidance; data extraction; SEM; bridge to triangulation; consensus meeting.
Version the existing DAG, extract assumption-relevant information, connect the SEM to the register, and prepare a SET-style input for triangulation.





Verbatim yellow-highlighted extracts — for template owners

The 25 highlighted paragraphs are reproduced without rewriting. The original Word drafts remain internal; a download of the proposed wording is provided below.

Associations v3.2 draftHypothesis-generating v2.2 draft



Research questions

Review mode and causal structure (recommended):
We recommend that you state the primary mode of the review: evaluating associations, hypothesis-generating, or a mixture of both. If any research question concerns mechanisms of action or hypothesised causal pathways, we recommend declaring this explicitly as a secondary (hypothesis-generating) mode.
We recommend that, in that case, you draw a scoping directed acyclic graph (DAG) at protocol stage: the variables of interest, the hypothesised directional links between them (including candidate mediators), and the outcome(s). The DAG is a working hypothesis, not a finding, and should be versioned (dated and archived).
We recommend that research questions about causal pathways are then answered edge by edge against the pre-specified DAG (i.e. “is the evidence consistent with this hypothesised link?”), rather than by reconstructing pathways after the findings.



Reporting bias

We recommend that, for each major bias, the likely direction of the resulting error is recorded relative to the relevant DAG edge (towards null, away from null, or unpredictable), in addition to the risk-of-bias judgement. Where quantitative bias adjustment is planned, the bias type can also be recorded: offset (additive) bias shifts every estimate by a roughly fixed amount and can create an effect where the true effect is zero, whereas scaling (proportional) bias inflates or shrinks estimates in proportion to their size and cannot.



Summary of the evidence

Making the Summary of Evidence (SET) table DAG-compatible (recommended):
We recommend adding the following fields to each row of the Summary of Evidence (SET) table: (i) which DAG edge(s) the evidence stream informs; (ii) up to three key assumptions on which the estimate depends, each typed as structural, identifying, indirectness or proxy, with status (agreed / contested / uncertain); (iii) the expected direction of each major bias relative to the relevant DAG edge (towards null / away from null / unpredictable); and (iv) a link to the versioned DAG and assumption register.
We recommend that the assumption register is seeded at protocol stage and versioned. Each entry records the assumption, its type, the evidence streams it concerns, its status, and what evidence would challenge it.



Triangulation meeting

Using the DAG and assumption register at the triangulation meeting (recommended):
We recommend that, before the meeting, each SET table row is mapped onto the DAG edge(s) it informs. Streams that inform different edges do not directly agree or disagree; any statement about agreement between them traverses an assumption (e.g. a proxy assumption) that should be named.
We recommend that conclusions are reported per DAG edge, with the traversed assumptions stated, rather than as a single global judgement.
We recommend that orthogonality is judged from the directions of the streams' major biases: streams whose biases favour findings in opposite directions (one towards null, one away from null) make agreement between them strongly informative. Representing each bias as a factor in the DAG makes this a checkable claim (the biases should share no common cause).
We recommend applying three revision triggers during the meeting: (a) evidence incompatible with a DAG edge; (b) an evidence stream that maps onto no edge; (c) an assumption challenged in discussion. Each trigger should lead to a versioned update of the DAG or assumption register.





DAG and assumption register

Versioning the DAG and attaching an assumption register (recommended):
We recommend that the DAG is treated as a versioned working model: it will be refined as evidence accumulates, and each version is dated and archived.
We recommend that, for each edge, you note which evidence streams (non-human, human observational, human interventional, mechanistic) can inform it.
We recommend attaching an assumption register to the DAG. For each assumption, record: its type (structural — an asserted causal link; identifying — what makes a stream's estimate causal; indirectness — how closely the stream's population, intervention and outcome match the target question, including animal-to-human relevance; proxy — a measured outcome standing in for the target outcome); its status (agreed / contested / uncertain); the streams it concerns; and what evidence would challenge it.



Data extraction

We recommend also extracting information relevant to the assumption register — for example the timing of mediator measurement, population characteristics, and intervention dose or exposure descriptors — so that indirectness and proxy assumptions can be re-evaluated as evidence accumulates, and not only effect estimates.



Summary of Evidence on Mediators (SEM)

Making the SEM DAG-compatible (recommended):
We recommend adding the following fields to the SEM for each candidate mediator: (i) which DAG edge(s) the evidence about it informs; (ii) up to three key assumptions (typed, and with status, as in the assumption register); and (iii) a link to the versioned DAG and assumption register.



Bridge to triangulation

Bridging to triangulation (recommended):
We recommend that, because this template produces a Summary of the Evidence on Mediators (SEM) rather than a Summary of Evidence (SET) table, teams preparing for triangulation derive a one-row-per-stream SET-style table from the DAG (using the fields described in the associations template) so that both template routes feed the triangulation meeting comparably.



Consensus meeting

Reviewing the assumption register at the consensus meeting (recommended):
We recommend that the assumption register is a standing agenda item: assumptions challenged by the accumulated evidence are re-statused (agreed / contested / uncertain), and the DAG is revised if a revision trigger fires (evidence incompatible with an edge; a stream that maps onto no edge; an assumption challenged in discussion).
We recommend that conclusions are reported per DAG edge, naming the assumptions they traverse. Note that a small mechanistic study that measures a node on a DAG edge can have probative value out of proportion to its precision, because it bears on whether an association is causal rather than confounded.

title: Proposal 3 · Reporting and the Summary of Evidence table
text:
The idea
The Summary of Evidence table (SET) keeps its existing columns for results, bias, indirectness, and other considerations. The proposed addition is a Key Assumptions column containing short typed statements or IDs, their status, and links to the DAG and assumption register. The register holds the detailed reasoning.

title: Proposal 3 · Reporting and the Summary of Evidence table
text:
Reporting the meeting outcome
The proposed wording makes the conditional interpretation explicit. For TAAR1, the key point is that a judgement about human symptoms cannot treat the animal proxy as the same measured outcome.







Situation
Suggested sentence structure




Contributions support the same interpretation
“Evidence from [streams] is consistent with [interpretation], conditional on [assumptions].”


Agreement may reflect shared bias
“The findings agree, but shared bias through [mechanism] remains a possible explanation.”


Contributions diverge
“The findings diverge for [relationship]; differences in [estimands, applicability, or bias] remain unresolved.”

title: LSR8 · Heat & Mental Health
text:
Priority adjudications



Issue
Why the decision matters




Medication use and social support
Their proposed roles may differ with temporal ordering; treating them as confounders, or shared causes of exposure and outcome, by default could change the quantity estimated.


Cooling-to-heat applicability (A7)
Determines the contribution cooling RCTs can make to the target heat question.


Ambient temperature versus extreme heat (A3)
Determines whether the two exposure constructs require distinct comparisons and interpretation.


Animal proxy and duration eligibility (A1–A2)
Determines what animal evidence is eligible and how it could inform human outcomes.


Depression and suicidality (A9)
Requires clarity on whether a line represents a causal hypothesis or a descriptive association. A correlation annotation is not a causal DAG edge.

title: LSR8 · Heat & Mental Health
text:
Applying the three proposals
As the Summary of Evidence tables (SETs) become available, use them to examine what each stream informs and which assumptions require revision.

Establish the baseline: record when the framework entered use, the available evidence, and which choices restate or extend the protocol.
Use the worksheet: record the interpretation, disputed assumptions, revisions, and actions through the four steps.
Carry the judgement forward: link the reported conclusion to the diagram, register, and evidence-summary versions used.



Supporting DAGs, selected assumptions, and evidence contributions

The five other original images support more detailed discussion. They are retained here as reference material.

Figure 3: Hypothesis diagram with animal proxy v1.1. Pink dashed connections represent proxy assumptions A1 rather than physical causal effects of animal outcomes on human outcomes.









Figure 4: Biological mediator detail v1.1. Candidate variable roles, including medication use, require adjudication.









Figure 5: Psychological mediator detail v1.1. Proposed links from the other mediator groups remain open for discussion.

Planned evidence contributions

Proposed role

Human observational studies

Quasi-experimental studies

What the design identifies and whether its quantity matches the target question.

Detailed questions for follow-up — evaluation

These are candidate observations for a pilot, not additional questions for the initial meeting.

Which assumptions or disagreements become more explicit, and do participants find that useful?
Does the contribution map change how a stream is interpreted or which conclusion is considered warranted?

Project materials and implementation details

The project materials include the completed protocol, draft DAG package v1.1, an assumption register, a provisional covariate-adjudication table, and a prefilled worksheet. The protocol records registration on 30 March 2026 (PROSPERO 1325620).
Evidence availability in those records is a dated snapshot. Current SET availability, the adoption date, meeting plans, and register ownership need confirmation with the review team. No effect estimates or meeting judgements are entered here.
The protocol makes convening a triangulation meeting conditional on sufficient evidence from at least two sources for an outcome. The register and evidence-gap record can be prepared before that condition is met.
